title: Handle a missing value
summary: NULL means a value is missing or unknown.
introduction: NULL means a value is missing or unknown. Your task: Choose a different fallback message.
learningObjectives: Explain the example for handle a missing value

blocks.text: NULL means a value is missing or unknown. NVL can supply another value when its first input is NULL.
Use Oracle Database 19c+ with a SQL editor in a new practice schema. Oracle SQL and PL/SQL do not run in this site's SQLite playground. Create only the named sample objects in that practice schema.

blocks.code: SELECT NVL(CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR2(20)),'Not chosen') AS book_choice FROM dual;
blocks.title: Handle a missing value

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `NVL` supplies its second value when the first is NULL. It does not mean that every missing value should become zero.
`DUAL` lets this Oracle statement return a calculation without an application table.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Test missing values with IS NULL, not = NULL. Missing is not the same as an ordinary empty label.
